name: First-Loss Criterion for a Corner Peeling
statement: Let nonempty ample $H$ have shattered complex $\Sigma$ and order $m=|H|=|\Sigma|$. For an ordering $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ and $D\in\Sigma$, define the death time $\delta(D)$ as the minimum, over all traces $q$ on $D$, of the last index at which $q$ occurs. The ordering is a corner-peeling order exactly when $\delta:\Sigma\to[m]$ is a bijection. Thus an order can be checked using only the original trace table, without constructing its descendant families.
proof: After the first $k$ deletions, a support $D$ remains shattered exactly when every trace on $D$ still has a representative, equivalently when $\delta(D)>k$. If the death map is bijective, exactly $m-k$ supports survive in a suffix of $m-k$ concepts, so equality in the Sandwich bound makes every suffix ample and every deletion a corner deletion. Conversely, a corner peeling has every suffix ample, hence exactly $m-k$ surviving shattered supports after $k$ deletions. These cardinalities force exactly one support to die at each time $1,\ldots,m$.
